name: Hairline
summary: Two skills that make isometric single-stroke line figures that react to the pointer, shipped as one dependency-free HTML file. hairline-create builds a figure from an idea; hairline-adopt rebuilds an SVG (icon, logo) as one.
why: Each buildlog project could get a living figure instead of a screenshot — Delivery Spec Validator as a sieve that lets the clean files through. And the skill itself is a lesson in pipeline-TD thinking: a fixed engine Claude may not touch, ten hard rules, a validator that rejects the page, and a look-check that screenshots eight poses before handing over.
caveat: Web interaction, not film motion graphics: it answers a mouse, it doesn't render to a timeline (you'd screen-record it). One visual language, so it suits a site that commits to that look. The look-check installs playwright-core once via npm.

name: Video Editor Assistant
summary: Eleven skills from a working editor: rough cuts from a timeline's own audio in Resolve and Premiere, multicam switching by audio correlation, cutting raw rushes to a client brief under a duration cap, and picking a music bed by measurement.
why: briefing-cut is literally your agency job — rushes plus a brief in, ordered selects under a cap out — and rough-cut-premiere lands a new sequence without touching the original. Scripts decide where splices land to the frame; Claude only decides what deserves cutting, and a report proves no word was clipped.
caveat: Filler-word rules are written for Brazilian Portuguese; you'd retune them for English and Hindi. Expects the open-source davinci-resolve-mcp repo installed alongside.

name: Better Writing
summary: Rewrites and drafts prose so it stops sounding generated, without inventing facts. Has a light-edit mode where every word starts as kept and a change needs a named failure. Eval-tested.
why: Applications, treatments and pitch emails are where AI-flavoured prose costs you most. It audits a voice sample before imitating it and marks missing facts instead of making them up.
caveat: Overlaps what Claude does when asked well; the gain is discipline, not a new capability.

name: Color Grade AI
summary: Measures a frame or clip, fits a correction by applying candidates and re-measuring, and emits a .cube LUT; detects log vs Rec.709 first and can match one shot to another.
why: Shot-matching bulk interview angles to a hero shot is real time saved; the measure-then-fit loop is a better idea than preset LUTs.
caveat: Your grading is judgement, and your Resolve connection already generates LUTs. Becomes an ADD if it learns to read your CST/ACES pipeline instead of assuming display-referred 709. Last updated August.

name: AI Video Storyboard
summary: Turns a brief into a multi-shot plan for videos longer than one AI generation, built on one good idea: consistency across shots beats any single perfect shot.
why: Right instinct for The Second Cup and the mythic film — a locked look bible before generating.
caveat: Pure prompt, no tooling, ad-and-reel shaped rather than cinematic. Needs a scene-to-shot grammar and per-model prompt formats to become an ADD.

name: H3 Storyboard & Performance
summary: Two thousand lines of measured findings on getting acting out of MiniMax H3 — which directions actually render emotion, with each rule marked by how it was verified.
why: The rarest thing in AI film: performance direction tested against output, not vibes. Composition-before-content is the spine.
caveat: Written in Traditional Chinese and tied to one model. Worth a translated read even if you never install it.

name: ffmpeg-skill
summary: 42 stdlib-Python FFmpeg tools behind one contract: probe first, edit, then check.py against a platform spec and look.py contact sheets before reporting. Covers lossless cuts, loudness to LUFS/true-peak targets, audio sync with drift fix, multicam, LUT and HDR-to-SDR, proxies, batch, and timeline export to FCPXML/EDL/OTIO.
why: The mechanical end of agency jobs (proxies for a folder of rushes, a -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP pass, a lav-to-camera sync, the same master cut down for Reels, Shorts and YouTube with a PASS/FAIL check on each) becomes one sentence to Claude with a five-line, measured report. It also writes an EDL or FCPXML you can open in Resolve or Premiere. It sits next to your delivery-QC app, it doesn't replace it.
caveat: Needs ffmpeg/ffprobe on whatever machine Claude runs it on. It is file-level only and doesn't drive Resolve or Premiere; video-editor-assistant (yesterday's ADD) covers those. The captioning and template defaults are aimed at social video. Transcription needs a local whisper/parakeet, which downloads its model on first use.

name: Director Master (山音超级导演大师)
summary: A gated five-step director workflow: tone, then rhythm plan, then script trims, then a shot breakdown, ending in a nine-column storyboard xlsx (shot no., timecode, angle, size, picture, location, sound, notes, narrative purpose). It has a rule to write only what the camera can see, and shot-length baselines taken from 551 shots of real shorts.
why: Turning a script into a shot-by-shot plan with a stated purpose for every shot is the prep work for the directing you're moving into. It pauses for your sign-off at each step instead of dumping a whole table at once.
caveat: Everything is in Chinese, including the trigger description, so it won't fire on English requests. An English fork or bilingual description would make it an ADD. MIT, pure markdown, nothing to run.

name: cinematic-director (DirectorSKILL)
summary: A director and previs skill. It turns a script, a brief or a single keyframe into a beat sheet, a director's book, blocking, a shot list with coverage and risk scores, keyframe prompts and image-to-video motion prompts, plus sound and edit plans. It also carries a coded failure manual (F1–F19) with a repair cost ladder and 20 optional director-style lenses.
why: It changes how he writes AI-video prompts and fixes failed ones. Each clip gets one camera move and one action that ends in a stated end state, and the same invariant text is repeated in every prompt. The prompt shape is picked to suit the tool (motion-only, full description, first/last frame, or timestamped multi-shot). A failure like 'face changed' or 'slideshow' maps to a code and the cheapest fix, instead of random re-rolls. It also covers the edit plan for cutting the clips together.
caveat: Markdown only, no scripts (about 11k lines of references, loaded only a section at a time). Most of each director-style file is in Chinese, with English summaries. The tool-capability tables are a 2026-08 snapshot and will go stale. It is clearly stronger than the four storyboard skills on WATCH, so those can probably be dropped. The history is one squashed commit, though it has a CHANGELOG at v2.1.0 and CI-checked evals.

name: after-effects
summary: Lets Claude drive After Effects on macOS. runner.sh uses osascript/JXA to make AE run an ExtendScript file, with arguments and results passed through JSON files. It ships 43 ES3 scripts: audits (project, missing footage, expression errors, fonts) and actions (relink footage, font/expression replace, comps from CSV, SRT import, batch render queue, incremental save), plus nine rule files on ExtendScript's limits.
why: Agency AE cleanup and versioning becomes a chat request: audit a handed-over project, relink footage from a new drive, swap a font across the project, conform fps or resolution on every comp, build lower-third variants from a CSV, queue 16x9 and 9x16 renders. Changes are wrapped in undo groups and risky ones dry-run first. It sits alongside his UXP and pipeline-TD work.
caveat: macOS only, and AE's 'Allow Scripts to Write Files and Access Network' preference must be on. The skill hard-codes ~/.claude/skills/after-effects-assistant but its folder is named after-effects, so fix the name on install. Scripts Claude writes for itself run without review except for operations it treats as destructive. runner.sh doesn't escape the script path, so avoid paths with quotes. One commit from March 2026 and none since. Total 16, so it misses the adoption bar of 17.

name: video-edit
summary: Turns raw 9:16 talking-head clips into a finished Instagram reel. It transcribes with faster-whisper, keeps the last clean take of each line in an EDL, assembles a CFR A-roll, adds HyperFrames/GSAP overlays and SFX, and checks every cut frame by frame inside the Reels safe zone.
why: The take-selection and dead-air pass on talking-head work: an EDL built from the transcript, plus a frame-accurate cut check on the render instead of scrubbing by eye.
caveat: Built around one creator's IG look (fixed looks, a hard-coded 'follow' insert, Apify scraping of his reels), and it renders HTML rather than producing an NLE timeline. Setup pulls npx hyperframes and remote SFX. It has no licence. It would be an ADD if the take-picking/EDL stage worked on its own and exported XML/EDL for Premiere or Resolve.

name: motion-video-director
summary: A director, motion-designer and sound-designer workflow for code-rendered video. Per-project taste and progress files, one beats.json driving both visuals and SFX, deterministic Playwright canvas renders, contact-sheet previews before export, and loudness/peak QA.
why: Promo or motion pieces for his own tools and clients: one cue file drives animation and sound, and references get broken into timed contact sheets first.
caveat: Commercial single-user licence despite the public repo, so he'd need to buy it or get the author's OK. It overlaps the installed animation skills. It would be an ADD if relicensed and proven on a real promo.

name: Remotion skills (official)
summary: Remotion's own skills for making video in React: 12 skills behind a router, including an editable Studio timeline, .cube LUT colour correction, FFmpeg silence detection and Whisper-WebGPU captions. Since 10-20 there's a version bump to 4.0.538 and one new render-performance rule (keep useCurrentFrame in the smallest component).
why: Data-driven titles, map explainers and caption burn-ins as code he can version and re-render, with an editable Studio timeline for client tweaks.
caveat: Unchanged from last time: it pays off only once he starts a real Remotion project, and then it is an ADD. There's no licence file. The Remotion License most likely applies, which is free for individuals and small teams. The skills are copied several times inside the router folder.

name: Check Skill (coder-eval)
summary: Builds labelled positive and distractor requests and measures whether a skill's description triggers it (precision, recall, F1). The repo's six commits since 10-20 are harness fixes (Docker, Codex, delegate). The check-skill folder itself is unchanged.
why: Puts a number on whether his own skills fire once the library grows and newer skills start dropping out of the listing.
caveat: Needs the coder-eval CLI, a sandbox and a paid agent run per row (16–24 runs). It overlaps skill-creator's own trigger evals. It becomes an ADD when he maintains several custom skills and sees misfires.

name: LintLang
summary: Deterministic offline linter for SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, tool definitions and system prompts. The skill is host-neutral, now pins lintlang 0.8.3 via uvx (which fixes a BOM-less UTF-16 file scanning silently clean and adds .cursor/rules discovery), treats scan output as untrusted, and says plainly that PASS doesn't mean safe.
why: A quick second opinion before publishing his own skills or the CLAUDE.md for his QC app or UXP panel.
caveat: Still heuristic, and the rules keep changing between versions. Leave the optional after-every-edit hook off. It becomes an ADD if he starts writing skills regularly and the rule set settles.

name: cold-email
summary: Cold outreach, now v2.2 with ten reference files and evals. The update moves it further into multichannel SDR operations: sending domains, LinkedIn automation, cadences by tier, AI-SDR reply triage.

name: Premiere Pro MCP: edit-premiere-project
summary: Operating skill for a local Premiere Pro MCP server: a CEP and UXP bridge with 436 tools. Claude inspects the timeline first, builds an edit plan, previews it, and applies it only with a one-time confirmation token. It reads the timeline back after each change, refuses raw ExtendScript unless asked, and checks exports frame by frame. Updated 2026-10-21; telemetry stays off unless you set a PostHog key.
why: Premiere work for agencies gets done from Claude: rough cuts and selects from transcripts, cleaning up bins and metadata (Scene/Shot/Take, ALE intake), verifying a delivery export against the spec, and OTIO/XML conform checks, all against the open project with an undo-safe preview first. It also sits right next to his own UXP command palette: same host, an MCP surface he can study or extend.
caveat: The skill does nothing without the MCP server and its CEP panel running on his Mac (installed with npx and opened in Premiere). That is a computer-side install of a large codebase I only spot-checked: endpoints, telemetry and the skill's safety rules, not all 880 files. The server's own plugin ships this skill, so install it from there instead of as a loose zip. That's why it isn't queued.

name: Screenwriting Skills (26-skill pack)
summary: 26 dramaturgy skills distilled from 47 craft books and 23 volumes of scripts: McKee, Field, Truby, Chekhov, Ozu, Japanese, Korean and French practice, series bibles, writers' room. Each skill is a numbered principle set with checklists, and a workflow skill routes between them. The bodies are in Chinese, but it answers in whatever language you ask in.
why: Script development for the features he wants to direct: diagnosing a scene that "doesn't turn" (McKee's value check, beats, enter late and leave early), premise and theme tests, and series-engine bibles. It argues from named sources instead of generic story advice, which fits his first-principles taste.
caveat: Not queued, for two reasons. The NOTICE carves the quoted book and script excerpts out of the MIT licence, so redistributing the pack isn't clean. And installing all 26 skills would put 26 descriptions on his shelf. Install it straight from the author's plugin marketplace, or pick sw-workflow, sw-scene-craft and sw-story-structure. About 850 KB of skill text in total, so expect heavy context.

name: video-use
summary: Edit by conversation from a word-level transcript. Claude packs the takes into a phrase view, confirms a plain-English strategy, writes an EDL, extracts each segment with 30 ms fades, adds overlays and burns subtitles last. Its hard rules for ffmpeg correctness are excellent.
why: Fast social cut-downs and talking-head edits from raw takes without opening an NLE. The take-picking and EDL logic is the reusable part.
caveat: Renders a finished mp4, not a Premiere or Resolve timeline. Transcription needs a paid ElevenLabs key. It overlaps the queued ffmpeg-skill and the video-editor-assistant ADD. It would be an ADD if it exported the EDL as XML/OTIO for an NLE, or ran local Whisper.

name: object-separation
summary: Local SAM 2.1 rotoscoping in one SKILL.md. It picks the model size from the machine, places the click points on a gridded frame, propagates in 60-frame chunks and writes a mask per frame plus a green-tinted check render. Nothing is uploaded.
why: Quick mattes for a product or person when Resolve's Magic Mask or Premiere's object mask struggles, or for feeding AE and compositing scripts.
caveat: Masks are computed at 960 px wide and hard-edged, so they don't hold up at 4K finishing. Output is a PNG matte sequence, not an alpha ProRes. It would be an ADD with source-resolution mattes, edge refinement and an alpha-channel export.

name: talking-head-editor
summary: Raw talking-head recording in, finished video out. DeepFilterNet voice cleanup with a capped reduction and a sync check to zero samples, Whisper in pause-separated chunks so retakes aren't merged, cuts that wait for a word's real end (it catches soft '-ts' and '-ence' tails), automatic face reframing with punch-ins, word-timed captions, and motion graphics written as pure render(t) code on HyperFrames with real sub-frame motion blur. Frame counts are asserted at every stage.
why: The talking-head jobs agencies send him (founder pieces, explainers, interview pulls). Take selection, pause tightening and the clipped-tail check become scripts with an audit he can listen against, instead of an afternoon of blade work. Each graphic is a small JS file, so a client note like 'faster' or 'rethink that one' means editing one function and re-rendering it, not rebuilding a comp.
caveat: It renders a finished mp4, not a Premiere or Resolve timeline. video-editor-assistant (10-17 ADD) is the one that lands cuts in the NLE, and this one is for jobs delivered as a file. Transcription is English-only (small.en), so Hindi needs a model swap. setup.sh pip-installs torch, whisper and DeepFilterNet into a venv, pulls GSAP from cdnjs and runs pinned npx hyperframes. It's a single commit from a new author, so it's young.

name: 超级峰的视频设计方法论 (chaojifeng-video-design)
summary: A Chinese-language director's method for explainers, product demos, launch films and music visuals: a story line and audience change first, then shot jobs, a sound event map, music cue selection by section, and a delivery record that keeps 'not watched / not listened' marked as unverified. Stdlib scripts validate the plan and measure a finished film (cut points, loudness, true peak, energy dips) and audit SFX hits against the event map.
why: Its film_probe and reference-film-study method (measure a reference's cuts, loudness and sound events, then separate what was measured from what was inferred) would help when he breaks down a reference spot for a client.
caveat: All instructions are in Chinese, and it is aimed at motion-design explainers and launch films, not his edit work. It would be an ADD if an English edition appears or he takes on product-launch or explainer jobs where the music-led planning pays off.

name: claude-real-video
summary: Lets Claude 'watch' a video: the crv CLI pulls scene-aware keyframes into 3x3 contact sheets plus a local Whisper transcript (optional speaker labels), and the skill reads the manifest and grids. It treats on-screen text and subtitles as untrusted data.
why: Breaking down a reference ad or a client's rough cut by asking Claude about it directly, with timings, instead of describing it by hand.
caveat: The skill is a thin wrapper around a pip package. The code shipped on PyPI isn't the repo you read, and the CLI upsells a paid 'pro' tier. Its --cookies-from-browser option (off by default, passed through to yt-dlp) reads browser login cookies. It overlaps video-use (WATCH) and the ffmpeg-skill contact sheets. It would be an ADD if the extractor shipped inside the skill.

name: Sepia (de-AI writing)

It splits work into write, review, refactor and recreate, uses a two-stage defect-list protocol, and has domain routes for fiction, journalism, release notes and tickets. It ships behavioural evals.
why: Rescuing a treatment, synopsis or festival statement drafted with AI: a defect list first, then minimal fixes, deepest layer first.
caveat: It overlaps better-writing (10-17 ADD), and you only need one. It's prose-only, with no screenplay format. It would be an ADD if it beats better-writing head to head on one of his treatments.

name: OpenCutAgent (premiere-edit)
summary: A Premiere Pro panel plus a local Node MCP engine that lets Claude edit the live timeline. It transcribes the source media, removes silences and fillers with a dry run first, and handles serial-restart retakes: Claude marks keep/cut per segment, you review the marks in the panel, then it applies them with cut points placed in the quiet between words. Big cut lists are applied through Premiere's own XML round-trip, so effects and transforms survive. Bundled skills: premiere-edit, remove-silences, setup.
why: This is the gap every earlier talking-head WATCH was missing: the cuts land in his real Premiere sequence, not in a rendered mp4, so he keeps grading and finishing in the NLE and Cmd+Z undoes any of it. Retake clean-up on raw interviews and VO is the first pass of most agency jobs, and this turns it into a reviewable keep/cut list. He builds Premiere panels himself, so the CEP host file and the bridge are worth reading as reference too.
caveat: This is an app, not a drop-in skill. It needs his Mac: a CEP panel with Premiere developer mode on (PlayerDebugMode), Node, ffmpeg, Claude Code signed in, and an ElevenLabs key for Scribe transcription (about $0.22 per hour of source, cached). An opt-in cloud mode sends media to the author's proxy instead; leave it off. Works on 100%-speed clips in flat sequences only, so no multicam or nested sequences. ppro_run_script runs arbitrary ExtendScript, and the README also offers a curl | bash one-liner; use the local ./install.sh instead. The licence is MIT plus Commons Clause, so it isn't queued here: install it from the repo on his machine.

name: boring-tools
summary: Edit video as text: cuts.tsv plus a per-shoot rebuild.sh are the project file. The chain runs VAD, per-span whisper.cpp, take grouping, face tracking on a square crop, eyeline matching across framings, measured subject edges for layout, wall-patch object removal, wall cards and captions, then verifies frame counts and A/V drift. Models are pinned by SHA-256 and the jobs run offline.
why: Cut-down sets from one take (15/30/60, vertical and landscape) where a client note means editing one number and rerunning, with the drift check reported each time.
caveat: Overlaps talking-head-editor (queued yesterday) almost entirely, and like it renders mp4s rather than an NLE timeline. It is macOS-only with VideoToolbox defaults and tuned to one creator's ad format. It would be an ADD if cuts.tsv exported to FCPXML/EDL for Premiere or Resolve, or if it did clearly better than talking-head-editor on take selection.
